decision.title: The built-in record types of F&O 4.0 (packet 2.6b)

body.p: . Accepts the Proposed items of and .

item.p: One table, declared once per registry: src/function_library_records.c lists the 16 nominative record types of F&O 4.0, appendix C (glossary ), each as its fn local name and the text of a structural record type in the specification's field order and types (a field whose type allows the empty sequence is optional, ; "xs:positive-integer" of fn:location-record read as xs:positiveInteger). sxml_function_library_initialize declares them in the type registry of its item heap before any row is resolved: all names first, so fields may name table types, recursion included, then each type's fields from its resolved text. A name the registry knows already is skipped, so libraries sharing a heap declare once. No globals; static analysis resolves fn:dateTime-record through the registry like any named type, and rows may name them.

Records are annotated: sxml_function_library_make_record makes a record of a built-in type by name (sxml_record_make). fn:parts-of-dateTime, fn:divide-decimals, fn:random-number-generator (and ?next), fn:regex, fn:matching-segments and its captured groups return annotated records; their rows name the types. The function items of a generator and of a compiled regex take their signatures from the record's field types, so ?take is fn(xs:nonNegativeInteger) as xs:double* (take(-1) and take(()) are XPTY0004) and ?next is fn() as fn:random-number-generator-record; fn:regex no longer looks its functions up in the function table.

Coercion to a nominative record type (XPath 4.0, section 3.4.2): the rule of a structural record type, the new record annotated with the nominative type (src/evaluator_function.c), so a map coerces to fn:division-record. Matching stays nominative: an unannotated map is no instance. fn:build-dateTime keeps map(*)? and its own coercion ().
idiv: a zero divisor is FOAR0001 before NaN or an infinite dividend (FOAR0002), so INF idiv 0 is FOAR0001 (F&O 4.0, op:numeric-integer-divide).

Measured (release driver, XP40, passed of cases): fn-parts-of-dateTime 8 to 20 of 20, fn-divide-decimals 19 to 21 of 21, fn-random-number-generator 50 to 54 of 61, fn-regex 27 to 29 of 30, fn-matching-segments 37 to 38 of 39, op-numeric-integer-divide 132 to 132 of 143 (wrong errors 2 to 0).
